questions.enonce_markdown:
The mass spectrum of a compound A has parent ion peak at m/e = 168. Elemental analysis shows that it contains 42.9% Carbon; 2.4% hydrogen and 16.7% nitrogen by mass. The remainder is oxygen

(i) Calculate the empirical formula of the compound A

(ii) Determine the molecular formula of the compound A

(iii) Briefly describe how you can test for the presence of Nitrogen in compound A. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Empirical formula.** Percentage of oxygen $= 100 - (42.9 + 2.4 + 16.7) = 38.0\ \%$. Take 100 g of compound (RAM: C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0, N = 14.0; the RAM of N is not printed in the useful data).

| Element | Mass / g | Moles = mass / RAM | Ratio (divide by 1.193) |
|---|---|---|---|
| C | 42.9 | $42.9/12.0 = 3.575$ | 3.00 |
| H | 2.4 | $2.4/1.0 = 2.40$ | 2.01 |
| N | 16.7 | $16.7/14.0 = 1.193$ | 1.00 |
| O | 38.0 | $38.0/16.0 = 2.375$ | 1.99 |

Whole-number ratio $\mathrm{C : H : N : O} = 3 : 2 : 1 : 2$.

**Empirical formula: $\mathrm{C_3H_2NO_2}$** (empirical formula mass $= 36 + 2 + 14 + 32 = 84$).

**(ii) Molecular formula.** The parent ion peak at $m/e = 168$ gives the relative molecular mass, $M_r = 168$.

$n = \dfrac{168}{84} = 2$, so the molecular formula is $(\mathrm{C_3H_2NO_2})_2 =$ **$\mathrm{C_6H_4N_2O_4}$**.

Check: $\mathrm{C_6H_4N_2O_4}$ has $M_r = 72 + 4 + 28 + 64 = 168$, with C 42.9 %, H 2.4 %, N 16.7 %, O 38.1 % (this is the formula of a dinitrobenzene).

**(iii) Test for nitrogen (Lassaigne's sodium fusion test).** Heat a small amount of A with a small piece of sodium metal in a fusion tube until red hot, then plunge the hot tube into distilled water in a mortar and crush it. Boil and filter: the filtrate (the "sodium fusion extract") contains sodium cyanide, $\mathrm{NaCN}$, formed from the carbon and nitrogen of the compound. To the filtrate add freshly prepared iron(II) sulphate solution, boil, then add a few drops of iron(III) chloride and acidify with dilute sulphuric (or hydrochloric) acid: a **Prussian blue** colour or precipitate shows that **nitrogen is present**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Write down the systematic name of each compound below.

(i) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3COH}$.

(ii) $\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3}$.

(iii) $\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_2CHCH_2}$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3COH}$: a tertiary alcohol, three methyl groups and an OH on the same carbon: **2-methylpropan-2-ol** (tertiary butyl alcohol).

**(ii)** $\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3}$: four-carbon chain with bromine on carbon 2: **2-bromobutane**.

**(iii)** $\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_2CHCH_2}$ (the double bond between the last two carbons, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH{=}CH_2}$): **pent-1-ene** (1-pentene).

(In (iii) the formula as printed has no "=" sign; it is read as the alkene $\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}$, pent-1-ene.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Under different reaction conditions, methylbenzene reacts with chlorine by different reaction mechanisms. One product of each reaction is shown below

![fig-1](gce-al-chemistry-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_5_fig_1.png)

(The scheme shows methylbenzene giving, in the upper reaction, the product with $\mathrm{CH_2Cl}$ on the ring (printed name "Chloro methyl benzene") and, in the lower reaction, the product with $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}$ on adjacent ring carbons (printed name "2-Chloromethyl benzene").)

(i) For the reaction leading to the formation of Chloromethyl benzene;

(A) Give the reaction condition

(B) Name the type of reaction mechanism involved

(ii) For the reaction leading to the formation of 2-chloromethyl benzene.

A: Give the reaction condition

B: Name the type of reaction mechanism involved *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Formation of chloromethylbenzene, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2Cl}$** (the chlorine replaces a hydrogen of the **methyl side chain**):

(A) **Condition:** chlorine gas with **ultraviolet light** (or strong sunlight), or boiling the methylbenzene while passing chlorine through it; no halogen carrier catalyst.

(B) **Mechanism: free-radical substitution** (initiation $\mathrm{Cl_2 \rightarrow 2Cl\cdot}$ by UV light, propagation steps, termination).

**(ii) Formation of 2-chloromethylbenzene, i.e. 1-chloro-2-methylbenzene (2-chlorotoluene), $\mathrm{CH_3C_6H_4Cl}$** (the chlorine replaces a hydrogen on the **benzene ring**, next to the methyl group; the 4-isomer is formed too):

A: **Condition:** chlorine with a **halogen carrier catalyst** such as anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ or $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ (iron filings), at **room temperature in the dark** (no UV light).

B: **Mechanism: electrophilic substitution** (the catalyst polarises $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ to give the electrophile $\mathrm{Cl^+}$; the methyl group directs the substitution to the 2- and 4-positions).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition reactions with HCN.

(i) What do you understand by a nucleophilic addition reaction?

(ii) Using ethanal, ($\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$) write the mechanism for the reaction with HCN.

(iii) Name the functional group present in aldehydes and ketones *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Nucleophilic addition** is a reaction in which a **nucleophile** (an electron-pair donor, such as $\mathrm{CN^-}$) attacks an **electron-deficient ($\delta+$) carbon atom** of a double bond, here the carbonyl carbon, and the double bond is broken so that the reagent is **added across the C=O bond**, giving a single product.

**(ii) Mechanism for ethanal + HCN** (catalysed by a trace of base, e.g. KCN, which supplies $\mathrm{CN^-}$):

Step 1 (slow): the cyanide ion uses its lone pair on carbon to attack the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon of ethanal. A curly arrow goes from the lone pair of $\mathrm{{:}CN^-}$ to the carbonyl carbon, and a second curly arrow goes from the C=O double bond to the oxygen. The result is an **alkoxide intermediate**, $\mathrm{CH_3CH(CN)O^-}$.

Step 2 (fast): the negative oxygen takes a proton from a molecule of HCN (or of water), with a curly arrow from an O lone pair to the H of HCN and the H-CN bond breaking to give back $\mathrm{CN^-}$.

Overall: $\mathrm{CH_3CHO + HCN \rightarrow CH_3CH(OH)CN}$, **2-hydroxypropanenitrile** (a cyanohydrin), a racemic mixture because the planar carbonyl group can be attacked from either side.

**(iii)** The functional group of aldehydes and ketones is the **carbonyl group, $\mathrm{C{=}O}$** ($>\mathrm{C{=}O}$): in aldehydes it is at the end of the chain ($\mathrm{-CHO}$), in ketones it is in the middle of the chain ($\mathrm{R{-}CO{-}R'}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is a functional group?

(ii) Name the functional group present in aldehyde and ketones. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A **functional group** is an **atom or group of atoms in an organic molecule that is responsible for its characteristic chemical reactions** (e.g. $\mathrm{-OH}$, $\mathrm{-COOH}$, $\mathrm{C{=}O}$).

**(ii)** The **carbonyl group, $\mathrm{C{=}O}$**.
